lead: the friendship began over a subject, and nineteen years on you ring him for the subject as often as you ring him for himself. he has never been sure which of them brought you.
sun: most people's interest in a friend narrows as it deepens — the subject that introduced you becomes furniture, and the person is what is left. The Claws forks it instead and keeps it forked. the questions about the work go on getting asked with the same heat as the questions about the marriage, year after year, and no part of you has ever ranked them or noticed that they could be ranked.
moon: the searching face finds a thing and moves off it, and the finding is where the pleasure sits. what it has here is two live scents on the same person, which never go cold at the same time. so the flat month that ends most friendships — the one where you have learned them and the appetite goes quiet — has not once arrived in nineteen years.
pull: he thinks one of the two is the real reason and the other is manners. both are the real reason, and neither has ever finished.
tension: two-way interest in a person reads, from outside, as one real interest with a cover story. his wife has him down as somebody you cultivate for the trade; two people in the trade have you down as somebody who got in through him. each reading is coherent, each is built on real evidence, and the evidence for one is the thing the other calls the pretext. explaining it out loud produces the exact sentence either of them expects.
cost: nobody has ever gone stale on you. nineteen years in, you are still the one who wants to know something, and the men he grew up with stopped asking him anything in their twenties. it also took you eleven years to be told what his oldest friend heard in a car park at nineteen. you came from two directions; the one who came from one arrived first.

lead: ninety people heard you defend him and ninety people heard you say what he did. it took three minutes, both of them went in whole, and the tape does not care which order they came in.
sun: you had two things to say and both were finished, arrived at over weeks, each costing something to hold. a room expects a position, which is one thing said with conviction. you brought two, at equal weight, with no ranking between them and no intention of supplying one — you said them one after the other, because a mouth can only do that, which put ninety seconds between the halves of a single position.
moon: The Storm does not wait for the second half. the first sentence landed at the size everything leaves you at, permanent on arrival, and the room had finished deciding about it before the second one started. so both are on the record at identical weight, and the ninety seconds between them is the only thing anybody has ever needed to hear one and treat the other as damage control.
pull: the first half of it was permanent before the second half was out of your mouth. both are on the tape, both were true, and every clip of you since is one of them.
tension: wanting it both ways is the phrase, and it arrived in that hall and has not left. the people who use it are describing an evasion, which needs one side of it to be soft, and neither was — they cost the same to say and neither can be taken back. his supporters play the first minute. the committee plays the last. nobody has played the whole three minutes to anybody, because three minutes is too long.
cost: a room that came in wanting one verdict left holding two, at the volume that makes a thing stick, and five years on both are still quoted. neither will ever be quoted with the other. you are the person who defended him, in one building, and the one who finished him, in another, and no version of that afternoon is short enough to correct either.

lead: neither trade has ever been told it lost you. you have gone back to the bench after nine years off it, and back to the desk after eight, and both rooms filed each absence as a leave.
sun: the two trades were never a first and a fallback. you qualified in both and have carried both since at working strength, which is why a return takes a fortnight — nothing was ever put down. what the arrangement cannot do is accumulate. every year given to one is a year the other is not being given, and no third place exists where the two totals add up into a career.
moon: the way back has always been open, and that is what keeps it running. each room holds the place, warmly, on the understanding that the absence was temporary — and it was, and so is the next one. nothing in you has ever registered a departure as final, so no exit has ever produced the conversation that would make either room stop expecting you.
pull: both doors opened again when you came to them, and both times the welcome was real. what neither room counts is the years you spent in the other.
tension: nobody who likes you can place you, and the word they reach for and put back down is settled. each room privately files the other as the affair — the place you go when this one gets dull — and neither has asked whether the other thinks the same. the returns keep being granted warmly, which stops it from ever becoming a crisis, and a crisis is the only thing that would settle it.
cost: you are the one either room calls when a job needs both trades, and you come back current, every time, with nothing to relearn. the people you trained in your first stretch are now deciding what happens to both. at fifty-one you have twelve years standing in one place and twelve in the other, and the person who picked one at twenty-four has thirty.

lead: you remarried in the third year, and you still say his name at the table every week without effort or ceremony. neither of those was a stage that the other one followed.
sun: grief is expected to be a sequence — a bad year, then a thinner one, then a life. yours went two ways from the funeral and has stayed that way since. one direction keeps him current: his sister on sundays, the tools oiled, his opinion still consulted on things he never saw. the other built everything that has happened to you since. both are full-time and neither was ever demoted to make room.
moon: neither direction has an edge on it. nobody, you included, can say how much of a week goes to him and how much to the people in front of you, because no total was ever struck and nothing in the arrangement supplies one. from any distance at all it reads as one thing — coping, or not coping, depending on which day the observer happened to be standing there.
pull: six years of carrying him and six years of building without him, at the same weight, in the same week. each one is what the other one gets accused of.
tension: his people watched you remarry and filed it. the person you married after him has found you in the car in his coat and filed that. each of them is certain they have seen the real state of it, and each has seen one entire thing and taken it for the whole. closure is the word both of them use, meaning opposite things. saying otherwise means producing the other one for somebody who will hear it as an excuse.
cost: his sister has somebody to be old with, and the two children you had after him have a parent who is not haunted, and neither of those was thinned to pay for the other. six years on you are nowhere near through it. the friend who widowed the same winter and went one way was done in eighteen months, and says so gently, every time.
